grade.why: Both candidates are identical to the reference patch, using the existing isArrayLike helper so array-likes are converted with Array.from and their length property is excluded.
Both candidates are identical to the reference patch, swapping isArrayLikeObject for isArrayLike in all three functions.

The two patches are byte-for-byte identical: both fix the mixed array/object branching correctly, but both copy the existing private isMergeableValue helper into each file instead of moving it to a shared _internal module.
Both patches make the same logic change (gating with `isIterateeCall` and moving `toString` after the guard check, which matches lodash's order), and differ only in where the import line sits.

Y also normalizes the media type in `bufferToFormData` (keeping the case-sensitive boundary intact), which the failing `buffer.test.ts` needs; X skips `buffer.ts` entirely, so that test will still fail.
Both patches are functionally identical to the reference; they differ only in placing the `stat` import at the top of the file and, in Y, using `filename += '/'`, neither of which matters.

Both fix `$url` query handling correctly, but X tracks the reference and only adds a sensible guard against a trailing empty '?', whereas Y also changes the WebSocket query-building path the task didn't ask for.

X matches the reference behavior by aborting on any `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype` segment, while Y blocks those keys only when the current value is a function, still skips `__proto__` instead of aborting, and makes an unrelated change to `zipObjectDeep`'s null handling.

Both handle null keys and values, but Y does it with a clear early return and `values?.[i]`, while X adds a convoluted length check with casts and non-null assertions that is harder to read and may add bundle size.
